records.title: Physics-Augmented Graph Transformer for Multi-step Time-Domain Maxwell's Equations in Electromagnetic Scattering
records.reason: Spatiotemporal modeling of electromagnetic fields governed by time-domain Maxwell's equations is essential for simulating and understanding wave propagation and scattering phenomena. However, accurate long-term predictions remains challenging due to the stringent numerical stability requirements and high computational costs inherent in traditional numerical algorithms. In this work, we present GT-MSMW, a novel specialized framework built upon the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) paradigm. To overcome the optimization difficulties of direct long-term mapping while mitigating the cumulative errors of step-by-step unrolling, GT-MSMW employs a robust blockwise forecasting scheme, advancing the simulation in stable multi-step intervals. A key innovation of our framework is the deep integration of physical laws: we design specialized edge features that encode discrete gradient and curl operators, guiding the graph neural networks (GNN) to learn the precise local coupled evolution. This local encoding is complemented by a Transformer module, which employs physics-informed distance gating to regulate the magnitude of spatial interactions based on spatial proximity, alongside self- and cross-attention mechanisms to explicitly capture the global couplings among electromagnetic fields. Validated on complex unstructured meshes, GT-MSMW demonstrates SOTA performance in 2D scenarios, significantly reducing rollout errors compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, the framework is successfully extended to 3D geometries, proving its capability to capture intricate wave scattering behaviors. Codes and data are available at https://github.com/0lin0-c/GT--MSMW.

records.title: U-EHR: A Self-Evolving EHR Agent with Step-Level Credit Assignment and UCB-Guided Memory Retrieval
records.reason: Large language model agents have shown strong promise for clinical decision support over electronic health records (EHR), yet current approaches treat tasks in isolation and lack capacities for self-evolution through accumulated experience. We propose U-EHR, a Unified EHR Agent with Retrospective Memory Evolution that enables continuous capability improvement through closed-loop experiential learning. U-EHR introduces three tightly integrated mechanisms: (1) Step-Level Trajectory Scoring evaluates each action in an execution trajectory along relevance, progress, and correctness dimensions, providing fine-grained credit assignment that distinguishes effective behaviors from detrimental ones within the same trajectory. (2) Dual-Polarity Memory Extraction transforms these quality signals into structured experiential knowledge by distilling both positive patterns worth emulating and negative lessons to avoid. (3) UCB-Guided Memory Retrieval formulates memory selection as a multi-armed bandit problem grounded in the Upper Confidence Bound principle, strategically selecting the most relevant memories from a growing knowledge base while exploring underutilized entries to prevent stagnation. As execution outcomes feed back to refine memory quality estimates and retrieval statistics, the three components form a self-reinforcing evolution cycle that continuously improves the agent's behavioral knowledge without external supervision. Extensive experiments on both the public MIMIC benchmark and our newly introduced Chinese clinical benchmark CN-EHR across diverse clinical tasks demonstrate that U-EHR consistently surpasses existing methods in accuracy and efficiency, with sustained performance gains as experience accumulates, validating the effectiveness of the proposed self-evolution paradigm. Notably, U-EHR exhibits strong cross-lingual generalizability on CN-EHR, suggesting that the learned experiential knowledge transfers across diverse healthcare environments.

records.title: Fine-Grained Structural Conflict Modeling for Compile-Time Instruction Scheduling on VLIW ASIPs
records.reason: Application-specific instruction set processors (ASIPs) often employ specialized hardware to improve performance, but this introduces complexity in resource management and programming. Existing compiler solutions, including LLVM’s default schedulers, lack fine-grained structural conflict analysis for complex arithmetic logic unit (ALU) instructions, leading to suboptimal performance or runtime errors. This limitation becomes critical when targeting very long instruction word (VLIW) architectures with instruction fusion units that exhibit pipeline-stage-level resource contention. In this paper, we propose a compile-time instruction scheduling method that models sub-cycle resource usage and analyzes both data and structural dependencies at fine granularity. Unlike coarse-grained resource tables used in existing compilers, our approach tracks functional unit occupancy at the pipeline stage level, enabling precise detection of structural hazards in complex execution units. We implement this scheduler as a backend pass in the LLVM compiler framework and validate it on the Sayram VLIW processor for wireless communication. Experimental results show that our approach achieves 100% scheduling correctness while improving execution efficiency by 23% on average compared with in-order scheduling, with benefits up to 38% for highly parallel kernels such as PRACH, and reducing average running time by 66% compared with atomic execution.
